sections.title: Sound of quê
paragraphs: The letter (quê) /ke/ mainly makes the sound /kw/, like in the word (quatro) /ˈkwa.tɾu/, which means four. This letter has two different sounds in European Portuguese.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air sharply while you round your lips into a tight circle. For the second sound, release the air without rounding your lips. Place a hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords stay still.

sections.title: Reading and writing
paragraphs: This letter always appears with the vowel u. Before the letters a or o, it sounds like /kw/, as in (quase) /ˈkwa.zɨ/. Before the letters e or i, the following vowel u stays silent, so the letter makes the sound /k/, as in (que) /kɨ/ and (aqui) /ɐˈki/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not add a w sound when the letter stands before e or i. English words like quick always keep that sound. In Portuguese, keep the second letter silent so it sounds like the k in keep.
